messages.subject: Re: About the dbWriteTable function in package RPostgreSQL
messages.subject_clean: About the dbWriteTable function in package RPostgreSQL
messages.body_plain:
Dear Zhou,

For later reference, the mails are sent to the rpostgresql-dev mailing list.
RPostgreSQL does have dbWriteTable().

> Another question: in the function dbGetQuery(connection, ‘SQL query’), the “COPY” command such as “COPY tablename FROM ‘file path’ WITH CSV” is not available?

I don't think "COPY" will work as a SQL.

A combination of internal function calls (not defined in DBI)

    postgresqlpqExec(connection, "COPY tablename FROM STDIN")
    postgresqlCopyIn(connection, filepath)
    rs<-postgresqlgetResult(connection)

should work if the file is of a proper format.
I'm not sure if "WITH CSV" works, but I guess it perhaps will work.

Note that the filepath does not refer to the path in the server, so the
client must send its content to the server.  
psql does the same thing internally and does not send the filename to the server.
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

messages.subject: r200 - r203 import libpq for windows from postgresql-9.1.1
messages.subject_clean: r200 - r203 import libpq for windows from postgresql-9.1.1
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Now libpq library source is copied to a subdirectory so that we can 
compile and distribute libpq.dll binary for windows platform.
Other platform continue to use the system libpq because we 
can't make libpq configured for every platform.

Because there is no functionality change, I think this should be released as
0.2-1.

PostgreSQL license only requests that the notice kept in all copy, and GPLv2
has a term (term 1) to keep such notice. So, distribution under GPL should be
ok for the libpq part.  In addition, if the libpq is separated from
the core, we can allow it to redistribute under the original PostgreSQL
license.  So, the License line of the DESCRIPTION would be
License: GPL-2 | file LICENSE

Best regards,
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan

messages.subject: Re: OS X ?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Dirk,

> Should I rework configure to that the internal source is used whenever
> pg_config is not found?

Thank you.

Making libpq compile on OS X required a bit of organisation change of libpq/
to prevent from confusion with the headers for windows.  But it seems to work now
with r211. (They are not made effective from top).

Perhaps it is better to use the copy when pg_config is not found or 
its architecture is incompatible to the current target.
That is, if the pg_config is 32 bit binary and we are to make 64 bit binary, 
we should use the internal code.

By changing the content of Makevars.in as
-----begin
PKG_CPPFLAGS=-Ilibpq
PKG_LIBS=-Llibpq -lpq

.PHONY: all
all:  $(SHLIB)
$(SHLIB): libpq/libpq.5.dylib

libpq/libpq.5.dylib:
	(cd libpq; make CC="$(CC)" CFLAGS="$(CFLAGS)" -f Makefile.darwin)
------end
compilation of libpq and linking against it can be enforced.
This file is not committed because presumably configure script should 
set necessary variables, which I do not know well how to do.

In addition to the configure change, we perhaps need to change install.libs.R

> Problem is, of course, that it builds three times (x86 32 bit, x64 64
> bit, ppc 32 bit) and I am not so sure how to keep configure layer sane.


We don't need to build three times.  
Universal binary can be made with
CC='cc --arch i386 --arch x86_64 --arch ppc'
It is good if we make the same combination as the R, anyway; having
more architectures than R binary is perhaps waste of disk space.
-- 
Tomoaki NISHIYAMA

Advanced Science Research Center,
Kanazawa University,
13-1 Takara-machi, 
Kanazawa, 920-0934, Japan

messages.subject: Re: RpostgreSQL install on Windows
messages.body_plain:
On 12 November 2011 at 11:59, Tomoaki NISHIYAMA wrote:
| Hi,
| 
| I wrote an instruction to install on windows in rpostgresql wiki.
| For 32 bit version:
| http://code.google.com/p/rpostgresql/wiki/WindowsInstall32
| and for 64 bit version:
| http://code.google.com/p/rpostgresql/wiki/WindowsInstall64
| 
| Note that this was written with very few experience and may contain errors.
| So, please let me know if you find something incorrect, not working, or
| missing.

A follow-up is in order here as Tomoaki not only provided this writeup, but
then proceeded to re-engineer the build on Windows, making the write-up
somewhat data: By shipping an embedded copy of the source of the PostgreSQL
connection code (which we can ship as it is of course Open Source), the
RPostgreSQL package is now no longer dependent on a PostgreSQL installation
in order to be built.

Hence, Windows binaries are back on CRAN, and Windows users of RPostgreSQL
can install a pre-compiled package just as they can for RMySQL or RODBC.

That is very good news which I detailed, along with more praise for Tomoaki,
in a short blog post a couple of days ago:

  http://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/blog/2011/11/21/#rpostgresql_0.2-0_0.2-1

RPostgreSQL is in very fine shape thanks to all his contributions. So three
cheers for Tomoaki!

Dirk

--

dark to read." -- Groucho Marx
